candidates.statement: In using the recursive form, note should be taken that, in general, the projection makes $U_k(X_1X_2)\not=U_k(X_1)U_k(X_2)$: one should store results for forests; not just for trees.
Recall that the sum of the $n$-th row in Table 2 must agree with that in Table 1, since each gives the total number of ways of partitioning the integer $n$.
Later we shall prove this result by considering the Connes-Moscovici restriction of the filtration of the bigrading of the full Hopf algebra.

Submitting $1,1,1,2,3,8,16,41$ to Neil Sloane's superseeker [@EIS], we learnt that it is generated by the first 8 terms of $$H_1(x)=\frac{R(x)-x}{R(x)}=1-\prod_{n>0}(1-x^n)^{r_n}. \label{H}$$ At the time, Sloane had no idea that we were studying the bigrading of rooted trees and told us "it is pretty unlikely this is your sequence, but I thought I should pass this along just in case".
candidates.section_title: Bigrading the full Hopf algebra of rooted trees

candidates.statement: We shall show that the latter are the key to the filtration $P_{n,k}$ of Table 4.

In the full Hopf algebra, we must show the existence of $P_{n,2}$ asymmetric pairings enumerated by $$P_2(x):=\sum_n P_{n,2} x^n =\dfrac12[H_1(x)]^2-\dfrac12H_1(x^2) =x^3+x^4+3x^5+5x^6+13x^7+28x^8+\ldots \label{P2}$$ Part of what is required is clearly provided by $$W(l_1,X)=l_1 X-2B_+(X) \label{WX1}$$ since ([\[BP\]](#BP){reference-type="ref" reference="BP"}) shows that $$U_1\circ W(l_1,X)=l_1\otimes X+X\otimes l_1 -2(P\circ B_+)(X\otimes e+e\otimes X)=l_1\otimes X-X\otimes l_1 \label{U1X}$$ has the desired antisymmetry.
Then s/he should contemplate the true challenge of quantum field theory, by recalling that -- in physical reality -- every node of every rooted tree may be decorated in an infinite number of ways.
